Module-driven C macro templates
==============================

An authoring unit imports a theory directly:

  (use-macros "Arithmetic.module" Macros)

The filename is relative to the authoring file. Imported module files,
including transitive theory imports, are ordinary make dependencies.
use-macros appears directly in unit. Includes and C preprocessor macros still
go to the selected native compiler.

The module uses Cesta's existing Module/Theory/Terms/Equations/Rewrites adapter:

  Module Arithmetic {
    Theory Macros() {
      Empty Terms {
        Twice . Expr ::= "(" "twice-once" Expr ")";
      }
      Equations {
        (Twice x) == (Macro "cesta-macro/1"
          (Profile "gnu11")
          (Arguments (Arg x (CType int) "value" (Evaluation "once")))
          (Result (CType int) "value")
          (Locals)
          (Template ("+" (Argument x) (Argument x))));
      }
    }
  }

Terms declares result and argument sorts. The equation supplies a versioned
contract and a structural template, not a string containing a program.
Quoted atom heads permit C operators and module-language keywords. String
and integer AST leaves are additive extensions of Cesta's adapter; this is
not a claim that the historical metta-venus reader accepts the extension.
Existing theory composition retains its declared origin profile.
Macro Terms is a constructor signature interpreted over the existing C
signature. Argument sorts such as DeclarationSpecifiers may be supplied by
that target signature. This extraction does not create a standalone textual
parser for the referenced C sorts.

cesta check-macros Arithmetic.module Macros checks definitions and emits their
structured contracts. Users add constructors and templates without changing
the C engine. Ordinary compact forms keep their meanings; a macro cannot
replace an existing compact head in the same result sort.

Supported contract fields
-------------------------

Profile is c11 or gnu11. The initial executable profile admits Statement
macros in C11 and Expr/value macros in GNU C. Portable C11 expression lowering
and additional syntax-result sorts remain to be admitted.

CType carries compact declaration specifiers and an optional declarator
template with exactly one TypeSlot:

  (CType int)
  (CType ("unsigned" long))
  (CType int ("*" TypeSlot))

The native compiler checks the resulting C types. Value arguments use
_Generic's value-context type. Addressable arguments compare pointer types,
retaining qualifications on the designated object. addressable-modifiable
also requires assignment to be valid. Non-addressable bit-fields do not
satisfy that contract. syntax arguments are unevaluated template syntax.
CType object size must be an integer constant expression.

Evaluation "once" evaluates each reached argument once, in declaration order,
and substitutes its saved value or place. "deferred" requires one template
occurrence and leaves its evaluation to the surrounding C control flow.
"repeat" includes an explicit template occurrence count; control flow still
determines which occurrences execute. "syntax" inserts unevaluated syntax
and requires the syntax category. These occurrence checks are not a proof
of arbitrary loop iteration counts or of behavior after nonlocal exits.

Generated native function-like macros prescan each supplied token sequence
before its use in admission and executable code. A separate result-admission
helper prescans the body before its type check and executable occurrence.
This keeps preprocessor effects such as __COUNTER__ from being repeated by
type checks. Statement and type arguments travel in shielded token tuples;
the native preprocessor removes those tuple delimiters at their sorted uses.
These are build-time helpers, not native runtime routines.

Clang's unevaluated-expression warning is suppressed only around generated
type/category admission expressions. Executable template diagnostics remain
enabled. Admission adds no runtime operation.

Binding markers
---------------

  (Locals (Local tmp "ordinary"))
  (LocalRef "ordinary" tmp)
  (Capture "ordinary" "caller_name")

LocalRef resolves to a declared slot identity. The definition checker uses
Cesta's existing C scope program to require one C declaration in the right
namespace, and rejects undeclared or multiply declared identities.
ordinary, tag and label binders use that admission. Member binders name the
record that owns them; see the version 4 declaration templates.

The native driver asks the selected compiler for an identifier inventory using
-E -dD, with the project's headers and flags, before emitting final fresh names.
This admission query remains private; exported C retains authored includes and
macro uses. The expander excludes written, module and admitted native names,
and emits guards against preprocessor macros with generated names. Arguments
containing opaque native fragments are refused by this profile. Unmarked
free expression identifiers in templates are refused; intentional caller
capture is explicit.

Definition-site ports, cesta-macro/2
-----------------------------------

Version 2 adds Ports between Profile and Arguments:

  (Ports (NativeSymbol absolute (SystemHeader "stdlib.h")
           (CType int ("function" TypeSlot int)) "abs"))
  (DefinitionRef "ordinary" absolute)

A used port includes its declaring header and captures the native C object or
function at the use-macros import point. The compiler checks its exact pointer
type with a static assertion. A caller's local declaration cannot redirect the
saved reference. Preprocessor aliases of the native name are temporarily
disabled while acquiring that reference, then restored. Unused ports emit no
header. SystemHeader lookup uses the native compiler's ordinary -I options.
If an earlier macro changed the native declaration itself, an unavailable or
incompatible entity is refused by the compiler.

Type parameters and compiler ports, cesta-macro/3
------------------------------------------------

Version 3 has the same outer fields as version 2. A DeclarationSpecifiers hole
with syntax category and syntax evaluation may be used as (TypeArgument t)
in CType or a template type position. Its use-site syntax is checked at that
sort; the native compiler checks the instantiated type constraints. For
example (CType (TypeArgument t) ("*" TypeSlot)) is a pointer to the supplied
type. Type arguments are not executable expression occurrences. They cannot
parameterize an import-level NativeSymbol port.

GNU profiles may declare (CompilerBuiltin conversion "__builtin_add_overflow")
in Ports and reference it with (CompilerRef conversion). This explicitly
denotes a compiler intrinsic rather than a caller binding or an addressable
native function. Native __has_builtin admission and preprocessor-name guards
reject unavailable or macro-redefined intrinsics.

This is partial hygiene admission. A finite native inventory is not a proof
about arbitrary preprocessor programs that manufacture identifiers depending
on the newly chosen spelling. The full native printing correspondence remains
open.

Declaration templates and record members, cesta-macro/4
-------------------------------------------------------

Version 4 has the same outer fields as version 3 and adds one result:

  (Result (CType void) "declarations")

at sort ExternalDeclaration. The template is a (unit ...) of ordinary C
declarations: records, typedefs and function definitions. Every argument is
syntax; Ports stays empty, because a declaration template names its C
dependencies through its arguments. (List a b) writes the headless list
(a b), as parameters and record members require.

  (Locals
    (Local record "tag" (Export name))
    (Local push "ordinary" (Export push_name))
    (Local data "member" record)
    (Local self "ordinary"))

Export takes its spelling from a CGeneralName argument: the caller chooses the
public names. An exported name must be a C identifier, and two exports cannot
collide in one C namespace. Every other ordinary or tag local is fresh.
A member local names the tag identity of the record that owns it and keeps its
written spelling, since member names are local to their record. The definition
checker requires each member to be declared exactly once, in that record.

  (Member data (LocalRef "ordinary" self))

Member is the only way to project a declared member, and its receiver is
explicit. The receiver must point to the owning record, with any
qualification; a different record that happens to have a member of the same
spelling is refused by the compiler. When the receiver is a parameter of the
enclosing function definition, the check is one static assertion on entry.
This holds for both spellings of a definition, (fn specifiers name parameters
body...) and the general (fn-shape specifiers declarator declarations
(block ...)). Elsewhere the check is an unevaluated expression at the use.
The checks add no instruction. A plain -> or . with a member local is refused.

Generated names are guarded against preprocessor macros of the same spelling.
An argument that hides opaque native source is refused. The emitted plan
records the use at position declarations.

A declaration family may add Contracts between Locals and Template:

  (Contracts
    (record (LocalRef "ordinary" record_type)
      (field (LocalRef "member" next) (callback (NameArgument next_type))))
    (function (LocalRef "ordinary" run)
      ("returns-borrow" 0 (LocalRef "member" ctx))))

Contracts contains ordinary ownership record, function or callback declarations.
LocalRef uses the same instantiated identity as the C template. NameArgument
uses one C identifier supplied as a syntax argument, such as a callback typedef;
compound types cannot stand in for a contract name. Quoted heads use the module
syntax's normal convention for hyphenated names.

An explicitly selected ownership check receives these instantiated declarations
alongside the caller's declarations. Identical declarations are deduplicated;
conflicting contracts are refused by the ownership checker. Without an ownership
selection the contracts add no checking requirement. Contracts cannot introduce
unchecked bodies or foreign assumptions. Generated bodies are checked normally,
and their actual permission plans use the existing admission path.

Formal and test boundary
------------------------

MacroTemplateNames proves structural symbol origin, local-marker reflection
under independent freshness, and preservation of exact named-context binding
positions across fresh frames. Kernel admission checks the actual template
slot bounds and occurrence counts from exported module data.
MacroDefinitionPorts proves acquisition and preservation of definition-site
declaration identities under independently admitted caller freshness. Actual
port registries and DefinitionRef requests are kernel checked separately.

RecordMemberNames states the naming law for record members: qualified by
their owner, distinct members stay distinct while different records may reuse
a spelling. It is a model law; actual declaration templates are checked by the
definition checker and the C compilers, not by kernel admission.

The native implementation, C type/category checks, ordered side effects and
object equivalence are tested separately with GCC and Clang. These results
do not prove the whole C compiler or establish the remaining hygiene joins.
